questions.question: Which river, flowing through the north-eastern part of India, is often called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its recurring devastating floods?
questions.explanation: The Kosi, a major tributary of the Ganga draining the Nepal Himalayas, frequently changes course and causes severe floods in Bihar, earning it the name 'Sorrow of Bihar'. (The Damodar is called the 'Sorrow of Bengal'.)

questions.question: Under the Constitution of India, the Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by:
options: A) the Prime Minister of India
D) the Chief Justice of India
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests the power of appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners in the President of India.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam, a classical dance form characterised by graceful, swaying feminine movements, traces its origins to which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam, literally 'the dance of the enchantress', is a classical dance of Kerala, rooted in the Devadasi temple tradition and performed typically as a solo recital by women.

questions.question: Which Indian state is the largest producer of coffee, accounting for the bulk of the country's coffee grown on hill plantations?
questions.explanation: Karnataka, with its Coorg (Kodagu), Chikmagalur and Hassan hill districts, produces roughly 70% of India's coffee. Assam is noted for tea, not coffee.

questions.question: The syncretic religious doctrine known as Din-i-Ilahi, which sought to blend elements of several faiths, was propounded by which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: Akbar introduced Din-i-Ilahi around 1582 as an ethical order drawing on Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism and Christianity; it attracted very few adherents, notably Birbal.

questions.question: Who served as the first Governor-General of independent India, holding office from August 1947 to June 1948?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten, the last British Viceroy, continued as the first Governor-General of independent India until June 1948; C. Rajagopalachari succeeded him as the first Indian Governor-General.

questions.question: The ancient Nalanda University, whose new campus at Rajgir was inaugurated in June 2024 as a revived international institution, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The historic Nalanda Mahavihara flourished in Bihar from the 5th to the 12th century CE. The revived Nalanda University, operational from 2014, opened its new Rajgir campus in June 2024.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the procedure for the impeachment of the President of India laid down?
questions.explanation: Article 61 prescribes the procedure for impeachment of the President for violation of the Constitution, requiring a charge by either House with a two-thirds majority and investigation by the other House. Article 56 deals with the term of office.

questions.question: The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027 is scheduled to be jointly hosted by which group of countries?
options: A) South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia
B) India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh
questions.explanation: The 2027 ODI World Cup will be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh co-hosted in 2023; Australia and New Zealand hosted in 2015.

questions.question: Who won the men's singles title at the Australian Open 2025, retaining the championship he first captured in 2024?
questions.explanation: Italy's Jannik Sinner defended his Australian Open crown in January 2025, defeating Alexander Zverev in the final in straight sets for his third Grand Slam title.

questions.question: Who won the gold medal in the men's javelin throw at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games with an Olympic-record throw?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem won gold with an Olympic record of 92.97 m; Neeraj Chopra took the silver medal with a best of 89.45 m.

questions.question: Who took oath as the 52nd Chief Justice of India in May 2025, succeeding Justice Sanjiv Khanna?
questions.explanation: Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai was sworn in as the 52nd Chief Justice of India on 14 May 2025, succeeding Justice Sanjiv Khanna.

questions.question: Which officer of the Indian Air Force became the first Indian to travel to the International Space Station as part of the private Axiom-4 mission in June 2025?
questions.explanation: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the ISS on the Axiom-4 mission launched in June 2025, becoming the first Indian to visit the space station and the second Indian in space after Rakesh Sharma (1984).

questions.question: In August 2024, India and which country signed the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) covering trade in goods, services, and investment?
options: C) Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)
questions.explanation: India signed a landmark Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement with EFTA nations (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland) in March 2024, covering trade in goods, services, and investment.

questions.question: The 2025 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to which Venezuelan opposition leader, honoured for her struggle to promote democracy in her country?
questions.explanation: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize to Maria Corina Machado, the Venezuelan opposition politician recognised for her promotion of democratic rights and the transition to democracy in Venezuela.

questions.question: Find the next term in the series: 120, 99, 80, 63, 48, ___
questions.explanation: Each term is one less than a perfect square, descending: 120 = 11² − 1; 99 = 10² − 1; 80 = 9² − 1; 63 = 8² − 1; 48 = 7² − 1. The next term is 6² − 1 = 35.

questions.question: Ship : Captain :: Aeroplane : ?
questions.explanation: A ship is commanded by its captain; in the same relationship, an aeroplane is commanded by its pilot.

questions.question: In a certain code language, DARK is written as EBSL. In that same language, how will GROW be written?
questions.explanation: Each letter of DARK moves one step forward in the alphabet: D→E, A→B, R→S, K→L, giving EBSL. Applying the same shift to GROW: G→H, R→S, O→P, W→X, i.e. HSPX.

questions.question: Pointing to a woman, Anil said, "She is the daughter of the only child of my grandmother." How is the woman related to Anil?
questions.explanation: The only child of Anil's grandmother is Anil's parent. The daughter of that person is Anil's sister (assuming the woman is not Anil himself, which the pronoun 'she' confirms).

questions.question: Ravi walks 4 km towards the south, then turns to his left and walks 3 km, then turns to his left again and walks 4 km. How far and in which direction is he now from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Facing south, a left turn points him east (3 km); another left turn points him north, walking 4 km — cancelling the initial 4 km south. Net displacement is the 3 km walked eastward.

questions.question: Three of the following four words share a common category. Which one does NOT belong to the group?
questions.explanation: Mango, apple and orange are all fruits; potato is an underground stem (tuber) — a vegetable — and so does not belong to the group.

questions.question: If ROSE is coded as 6821, CHAIR as 73456 and PREACH as 961473, then what is the code for SEARCH?
questions.explanation: From the codes: R=6, O=8, S=2, E=1, C=7, H=3, A=4, I=5, P=9. Hence SEARCH = S2 E1 A4 R6 C7 H3 = 214673.

questions.question: In an examination, a student who secured 180 marks obtained exactly 45% of the maximum marks. What is the maximum number of marks for the examination?
questions.explanation: 45% of maximum = 180, so maximum = 180 × 100/45 = 400.

questions.question: An amount of ₹1,200 is divided among three friends A, B and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. What is the share of C?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 2+3+5 = 10. One part = 1200/10 = 120. C's share = 5 × 120 = ₹600.

questions.question: A and B working together can finish a task in 6 days. A alone can finish it in 10 days. In how many days can B alone finish the task?
questions.explanation: B's one-day work = 1/6 − 1/10 = (5−3)/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. So B alone needs 15 days.

questions.question: A trader sells an article for ₹720 and incurs a loss of 10% on the cost price. What was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 90% of cost price, so CP = 720 × 100/90 = ₹800.

questions.question: A train 200 metres long completely crosses a platform 300 metres long in 25 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanation: To clear the platform the train covers 200 + 300 = 500 m in 25 s, i.e. 20 m/s. Speed = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum at 6% per annum for 3 years is ₹540. What is the sum?

At the time of marriage, a husband and a wife were both 25 years old. A child was born two years after their marriage. What is the average age of the family (the three members) eight years after the marriage?
questions.explanation: Eight years after marriage, the husband and wife are 33 each and the child is 8 − 2 = 6 years old. Average = (33+33+6)/3 = 72/3 = 24 years.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2^20 is divided by 7?
The 400 students of the senior wing of a school are distributed across four streams as follows — Science: 130; Commerce: 110; Arts: 100; Vocational: 60. What percentage of the students study Science?
questions.explanation: Science students = 130 out of 400, so percentage = 130/400 × 100 = 32.5%.

questions.question: If x + y = 10 and xy = 21, what is the value of x² + y²?
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the measure of the largest angle?
questions.explanation: Sum of parts = 9, so one part = 180°/9 = 20°. The largest angle = 4 × 20° = 80°.

questions.question: A bakery's annual revenue was ₹4.8 lakh in 2023 and ₹6.0 lakh in 2024. What was the percentage increase in revenue from 2023 to 2024?
questions.explanation: Increase = 6.0 − 4.8 = ₹1.2 lakh. Percentage increase = 1.2/4.8 × 100 = 25%.

questions.question: If a − b = 4 and ab = 12, what is the value of a + b?
questions.explanation: (a+b)² = (a−b)² + 4ab = 16 + 48 = 64, so a + b = 8 (taking the positive root, as the sum's magnitude is fixed at 8).

questions.question: A closed cylindrical water tank has a radius of 7 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Volume of a cylinder = πr²h = (22/7) × 7² × 10 = 22 × 7 × 10 = 1,540 cubic cm.

questions.question: In a survey of 5,400 students, the favourite pastime of each student was recorded and shown in a pie chart with the following central angles — Music: 90°; Reading: 72°; Sports: 120°; Painting: 48°; Others: 30°. How many more students chose Sports than Painting?
questions.explanation: Angles total 90+72+120+48+30 = 360°. Each degree represents 5,400/360 = 15 students. Difference in angles = 120° − 48° = 72°, so 72 × 15 = 1,080 students (Sports 1,800; Painting 720).

questions.question: Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. Some flowers are roses. Which conclusion(s) follow?
options: A) Neither conclusion I nor II follows
B) Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: II follows directly: 'All roses are flowers' implies some flowers are roses. I does not follow — the red flowers need not include any rose, since 'some flowers are red' does not tell which ones.

questions.question: Four friends L, M, N and O are sitting in a row facing north. M is at the extreme left; L sits immediately to the right of M; N sits at the extreme right; O sits between L and N. Who is second from the left end?
questions.explanation: The arrangement from left to right is M, L, O, N. The second seat from the left is occupied by L.

questions.question: If 1 January 2026 falls on a Thursday, on which day of the week will 1 February 2026 fall? (2026 is not a leap year)
questions.explanation: January has 31 days; 31 mod 7 = 3. So 1 February falls 3 weekdays after Thursday, which is Sunday.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:20?
questions.explanation: At 4:20 the minute hand is at the 4 (120° from 12); the hour hand has moved 4×30 + 20×0.5 = 130°. The angle between them is 130° − 120° = 10°.

questions.question: Statements: No cats are dogs. All cats are mammals. Conclusions: I. Some mammals are not dogs. II. No mammals are dogs. Which conclusion(s) follow?
options: B) Both conclusions I and II follow
D) Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Every cat is a mammal and no cat is a dog, so at least the mammals that are cats are not dogs — conclusion I follows. II is wrong because mammals other than cats may be dogs.

questions.question: Five teachers — Anand, Beena, Charu, Dev and Ela — each take their activity period on a different weekday from Monday to Friday. Beena's period is on Wednesday; Anand's period is immediately after Beena's; Charu's period is on Monday; and Ela's period is not on Friday. Who takes the period on Tuesday?
questions.explanation: Monday: Charu; Wednesday: Beena; Thursday: Anand (immediately after Beena). Ela is not on Friday, so Ela takes Tuesday and Dev takes Friday.

questions.question: Three friends — Amit, Bharat and Chetan — live in three different cities: Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai, and each has a different profession: Teacher, Engineer and Doctor. Given that: (1) Bharat is the Doctor; (2) the Engineer lives in Mumbai; (3) Amit lives neither in Chennai nor in Mumbai; (4) Chetan does not live in Delhi. Who is the Engineer?
questions.explanation: Amit lives in Delhi (clue 3), so Chetan, not living in Delhi (clue 4), lives in Mumbai — and the Engineer lives in Mumbai (clue 2), so Chetan is the Engineer. That leaves Bharat as the Doctor in Chennai, consistent with clue 1.

questions.question: Which vitamin is synthesised in human skin in the presence of sunlight and is essential for the absorption of calcium?
questions.explanation: The skin produces vitamin D when ultraviolet-B rays in sunlight act on a cholesterol derivative; vitamin D aids intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphorus.

questions.question: Which plant tissue is responsible for conducting water and dissolved mineral salts from the roots up to the leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels carry water and minerals upward from roots to leaves; phloem transports prepared food, mainly downward from leaves.

questions.question: India's 'Blue Revolution', launched to boost production through modern technology and infrastructure, is associated with which sector?
questions.explanation: The Blue Revolution refers to the modernisation and expansion of India's fisheries and aquaculture sector; the White Revolution relates to milk and the Green Revolution to food grains.

questions.question: The rusting of iron, a common example of corrosion, essentially requires the presence of:
options: A) both oxygen and water vapour
questions.explanation: Rusting is the formation of hydrated iron(III) oxide, which needs both oxygen and moisture; in completely dry air or in boiled water with an oil layer, iron does not rust appreciably.

questions.question: The gradual and progressive replacement of one ecological community by another in a barren area over time, culminating in a stable community, is called:
questions.explanation: Ecological succession is the ordered, gradual change in the species structure of a community over time — from pioneer species to a climax community; eutrophication is nutrient over-enrichment of water bodies.

questions.question: According to the 10% law of energy transfer in a food chain, if the producers in an ecosystem store 20,000 J of energy, how much energy will be available to the tertiary consumers?
questions.explanation: Only 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level: producers 20,000 J → primary consumers 2,000 J → secondary consumers 200 J → tertiary consumers 20 J.
